extracted.intended_audience: Organizations and individuals seeking ACL grant funding (state/local governments, nonprofits, institutions of higher education, small businesses), current grantees, and prospective peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Overview guidance on ACL (Administration for Community Living) grant types, eligibility, where opportunities are announced, and basic administration/management expectations for applicants and grantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory (or Formula) Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mandatory, or 'formula,' grants are on-going programs, which require no application or competition. Eligibility and funding levels for mandatory grants are based on legislation which often uses a formula to determine the allocation of grant funds across eligible entities (such as states, tribes, territories, and other organizations specified by legislation)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details about mandatory/formula grant allocations are provided on the site; for questions see the programmatic and fiscal contacts list. Administrative/management resources referenced include the Mandatory/Formula Grants Module in GrantSolutions and the ACL Process to Request a Change in Key Personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary (or Competitive) Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: "Discretionary, or 'competitive,' grants allow ACL to exercise discretion in selecting the projects to be funded and determining the amount of the award."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once awarded, discretionary grants provide grantees with significant flexibility and control over how grant objectives are achieved (within the scope of the approved application). If substantial ACL involvement is required, the award may be administered as a cooperative agreement. ACL announces competitive opportunities via the Funding Opportunities section and Grants.gov; each FOA contains all information needed to apply. For FOA-specific questions, contact the designated program staff listed in the FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative Agreement when Substantial ACL Involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the nature of the grant requires substantial ACL involvement, ACL will administer the grant as a cooperative agreement, which affords the agency a role in grant decisionmaking."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note that awards administered as cooperative agreements differ from standard discretionary grants by including an active ACL role in decisionmaking and project oversight; this affects expectations for collaboration and management during the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Recipient Types
rubrics_metrics.description: "ACL awards more than one billion dollars in grants, primarily to state and local governments, nonprofit organizations, institutions of higher education and small businesses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACL funds states and organizations that provide services and supports for older adults and people with disabilities, conduct research, and develop innovative approaches. Eligibility specifics depend on the statutory program (particularly for mandatory/formula grants) or the FOA (for discretionary grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: FOA Contains All Application Information
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each FOA contains all information needed to apply for a grant."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants must consult the Funding Opportunity Announcement for application requirements, submission instructions, deadlines, eligibility, and evaluation criteria. FOAs are posted on ACL's Funding Opportunities page and on Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Administration and Management Resources / Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: References to post-award administrative guidance such as "Drawdown Memorandum to Grantees of ACL Discretionary Grants," "Drawdown Memorandum to Grantees of ACL Mandatory/Formula Grants," "Drawdown Memorandum to Grantees of ACL Older Americans Act State Unit on Aging Grants," and "Notification of Retirement of FCTRs in PMS."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site points applicants and grantees to the 'Managing a Grant' section for information on managing an ACL grant. Specific administrative processes include drawdown procedures, payment system changes, and the ACL Process to Request a Change in Key Personnel. Use the appropriate GrantSolutions module for mandatory/formula grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to Find Past Award Information
rubrics_metrics.description: "Information regarding past awards can be found at www.usaspending.gov."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can review past ACL awards on USAspending.gov to inform competitive application development, understand typical award amounts, and identify funded project types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity Announcement and Questions Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL announces competitive (discretionary) grant funding opportunities through the Funding Opportunities section and at www.Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For questions about specific grant opportunities, applicants should contact the designated program staff indicated in the Funding Opportunity Announcement. The FOA is the authoritative source for application instructions and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation as a Peer Reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: "Learn how to become a peer reviewer for ACL."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site invites qualified individuals to serve as peer reviewers, implying a formal review process for discretionary grants and an opportunity for practitioners to participate in evaluation of applications; details are available through the linked guidance.
